items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: So I called Coleman. I said, "Coleman, would you do a recording date with me?' He said, "Yeah."

ctx.x: said, "Well, I'll check it out." So I called Coleman. I said, "Coleman, would you do a recording date with me?' He said, "Yeah." I said, "How much you want?" He said, "I'll do it for a hundred dollars a day." Well, that was so cheap, I think I told him "yeah" then. I didn't even check with Joe Davis, but I knowed that would be all right. And that's when I got him after Ben Webster. Because I was always changing my personnel.

Then after he did the date with me, we made a date with just him... I wish I could get ahold of them records. I wrote four tunes for him. And all I did was write the progressions. See, because he was a master at progression. And me being a saxophone player, I knew the different progressions that saxophone players like. They love the modulation of the fifth, and they can go into any change and go into the fifth. So I just made different changes... And one thing I give Joe Davis credit for, he could give a name to…
